description:
Goal: move the definition lifecycle onto a clearer arrangement of responsibilities. The bootstrap (runtime.fz and the runtime library modules) is the only code that deserves special treatment. Everything else follows one model: index a submission, define a module by expanding module-scope macros down to the Compiler.define boundary (use and other definition-generators run here, at define time), note members as raw unexpanded sources, then expand a body only when it is referenced. A definition carries the lexical env it was created in, the same way Elixir caches env at def time.

Why now: investigation under this epic proved the apparent over-broad Kernel source publication is correct stock-taking, not waste. The real defects are two model conflations. FunctionEnvSource threads projected-vs-carried env where the boundary is bootstrap-vs-macro-origin. ScopeSurfaceMode threads source-vs-fragment where the boundary is pre-vs-post-expansion with the bootstrap as the lone exception. We project an __ENV__ at definition and discard it after one telemetry read; nothing makes def-site __ENV__ available to a body. Patching either mode in isolation deepens the conflation; moving the responsibilities dissolves both.

Grounded findings:
- Tiny x + 1 notes all 58 Kernel members (function.source.noted) but expands only 6 (function.source.expanded); define/lower/activate are equally narrow. The broad tier is correct raw-AST stock-taking.
- ensure_function_source for a non-global module demands DefineModule(module), which publishes the whole module surface. This is the intended scope-defines-all behavior (northstar worked example), not a bug.
- semantically_eq ignores namespace-ids; source_same already compares the namespace BindingId field, so namespace stability is an existing idempotency invariant. The captured env is a pure projection of {module, function, namespace} already in FunctionSource, so it is a derived cache and must be excluded from source_same.
- project_env_value and project_module_value are &self and force nothing; eager env capture leaks no laziness.
- build_form (quoted_surface.rs:354) is the only mode-dependent branch: Source treats fn/fnp/defmacro/defmodule/defprotocol/defimpl heads as macro-calls; CompilerFragment treats them as direct definitions. Protocol and impl bodies read as fragments because they are post-expansion.
- runtime.fz defmacro fn/fnp/defmacro/defmodule/defprotocol/defimpl all expand to Fz.Compiler.define(source, __CALLER__); user defs are genuinely macro-driven, while the bootstrap is parsed canonically.

Outcome: delete FunctionEnvSource, ScopeSurfaceMode, the throwaway env projection, and the is_runtime_prelude/is_runtime_module_code synonym sprawl. Add env to FunctionSource (derived cache) and a def-site __ENV__ binding at expansion. The remove column outweighs the add.

Decomposed into fz-rh2.28.1 through fz-rh2.28.5, executed in dependency order.

comments.text: Child ordering: the second step (phase vs origin) is fz-s00, adopted in place of a deleted fz-rh2.28.2 because fz-s00 already carries the deeper, correct framing (one source read; def-head structure emerges from the define pipeline, not a mode-gated re-parse). DAG: fz-rh2.28.1 -> fz-s00 -> fz-rh2.28.3 -> fz-rh2.28.4 -> fz-rh2.28.5.

title: Compiler2 definition lifecycle: bootstrap is the only exception, carry the definition env, separate phase from origin
